text:
Alex M: Quick sketch — proposing a small state-machine to formalize delegation between the pool orchestrator and the autoscaler. Idea: orchestrator = topology owner (nodes, shards, long-running reservations); scaler = short-lived admission/lease manager and headroom adjustments. Trying to avoid repeated race conditions we saw last week.

Alex M: Sketch states: IDLE -> PROBING -> PREWARM -> ACTIVE -> DRAIN. Events: demand_increase, demand_decrease, probe_timeout, prewarm_ready, node_evicted. Ownership: orchestrator transitions nodes between AVAILABLE/HELD/RETIRING, scaler requests LEASEs with TTLs and can escalate to PREWARM when tail-latency spikes.

Alex M: Tiny ascii: 
```
Orch: node pool {AVAILABLE, HELD, RETIRING}
Scaler: lease {REQUESTED, GRANTED(t=TTL), PREWARMING, ACTIVE}
Events: request -> orch.grantLease -> scaler.prewarm -> scaler.activate -> usage drops -> scaler.release -> orch.retire
```

Priya S: This reads well. Two quick q's: 1) who owns the final decision to evict when leases collide? 2) how do we surface metric windows for probe -> prewarm?

Alex M: Good q. eviction decision stays with orchestrator (global safety). Scaler can mark a lease as "urgent" with a preempt_priority flag but orch enforces fairness policies. For probe->prewarm threshold: use 95p latency over a rolling 30s window + token throughput delta > X. Configurable per-tenant.

Marco G: Concern: what about burst lanes and reserved credits? If scaler asks for PREWARM and orch is short on headroom, we don't want to degrade other tenants. Suggest adding an AdmissionStatus: {ALLOW, THROTTLE, QUEUE_FOR_BURST}. Orch replies with reason code to scaler so scaler can fallback to smaller model.

Alex M: Yes agreed — AdmissionStatus was on my next slide. Reason codes like "insufficient_headroom", "preemption_window", "quota_exhausted". Scaler should have policy hooks: fallback_model(), degrade_batch_size(), or queue.

Jen L: Observability: we need a single correlation id for each lease lifecycle so Console can show where time was spent (grant latency, prewarm time, activation). Proposed fields: lease_id, request_ts, grant_ts, prewarm_complete_ts, active_ts, release_ts. Also emit lease.owner and lease.priority.

Priya S: +1 on correlation id. Also can we emit the orch decision rationale string field for postmortem debugging? (e.g., "granted: headroom 2 GPUs, reserved credits 0.7")

Alex M: Yeah add decision_rationale text. Keep it short (<=256 chars).

Marco G: Edge case: what happens during drain when an ACTIVE lease is still in use because client hasn't returned KV cache? We should allow a GRACE_EXTEND event that orch can honor up to a max_grace_per_tenant. Also need a hard cutoff to avoid zombie consumption.

Alex M: Plan: scaler sends release intent; orch can respond with {ACK, ACK_WITH_GRACE(ms), FORCE_EVICT}. Force evict triggers cached-KV flush metric and a fallback route. Documenting that in the SLA.

Jen L: Does this change the autoscaler control loop frequency? If scaler has to probe more often, we risk noisy scaling. Maybe introduce a cool-down on probe->prewarm per-tenant (e.g., 60s) and exponential backoff on failed prewarms.

Alex M: Agreed. Add probe_cooldown and failed_prewarm_backoff params. Default probe_cooldown=45s.

Priya S: Quick ask: can we add a small RPC contract sketch? Something like: 
```
RequestLease(tenant_id, demand_estimate) -> {status, lease_id, ttl_ms, admission_status, decision_rationale}
KeepAlive(lease_id) -> {status, new_ttl_ms}
Release(lease_id, reason) -> {status}
OrchEvent(stream) -> events: {lease_granted, lease_revoked, headroom_change}
```

Alex M: Exactly what I had in mind. I'll add a proto draft to the RFC.

orch-bot: autoscaler-staging: test rollout succeeded for branch "state-machine-lease". :rocket:

Marco G: One more: telemetry cost accounting. When orch grants a lease, tag short-term tokens to that lease for billing. That way we can reconcile prewarm CPU/GPU amortization.

Alex M: Nice. We'll fold that into the billing tags.

Priya S: OK next steps from my side: I'll write a PoC for the lease RPC + a unit test that simulates contested leases. Marco, can you do a simulation for burst scenarios? Jen, can you wire the lease lifecycle traces into Console mocks?

Marco G: Yup can run sim next week.

Jen L: On it — will add panels and a simple flamechart mapping lease phases.

Alex M: I'll author a short follow-up RFC with the proto + state diagrams and add the config knobs we mentioned. Targeting review by EOW. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
